items.description: Australia would be the "perfect" target for a fledgling Islamist terror network that has carried out antisemitic attacks in Europe, the UK and Canada, experts have warned.

items.title: Blast at explosives storage site kills dozens in Myanmar

featured_image.name: Blast kills dozens in village in rebel-held region of Myanmar

items.description: An explosion at a building storing mining explosives in northeastern Myanmar killed at least 46 people on Sunday, including six children, with local media reporting death tolls as high as 55. About 70 others were injured in the blast, which struck around noon in the village of Kaungtup in Namhkam township, roughly two miles from the Chinese border.

items.title: Young Australians reject budget as One Nation popularity climbs further
items.description: Labor's federal budget is falling flat with its target demographic as millennials say they'd rather vote for One Nation than Labor or the Greens, according to a new Redbridge poll.

items.description: Israeli troops have captured a strategic mountain topped with a Crusader-built castle in southern Lebanon, in their deepest incursion into the country in decades.

items.title: Australia scraps new Virginia-class submarines in AUKUS shake-up
items.description: The US, UK and Australia have announced they will "streamline" the purchase, with Australia no longer buying new submarines, and acquiring three second-hand ones.

items.title: Lula rejects U.S. terrorist label for Brazil's largest gangs

featured_image.name: Lula blasts US for labelling Brazil crime factions as terrorists

items.description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Friday denounced the United States' decision to designate two of Brazil's largest criminal organizations as terrorist groups, calling it undue interference in the country's internal affairs and warning Washington against treating Brazil "like a banana republic."

"We will not accept being treated like children, we will not accept being treated as if we were a banana republic," Lula said at a public event on Friday, referring to "a certain Marco Rubio, who said that our criminals are terrorists and that Americans can intervene".[1][2]

items.title: Philippines says China threat persists despite Trump-Xi summit

featured_image.name: Philippines defence chief Gilberto Teodoro Jr calls out China's 'propaganda  spiel' at Shangri-La Dialogue | The Straits Times

items.description: The Philippines' defense secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said on Saturday that the country remains under "severe threat" from China, declaring that a recent thaw in U.S.-China relations following the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing has done nothing to ease tensions in the South China Sea.[1][2]

items.title: Quarter of trapped oil tankers slip out of Hormuz

featured_image.name: A Quarter of Large Oil Tankers Trapped by Iran War Have ...

items.description: A slow, stealthy trickle of oil tankers has begun slipping out of the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, with roughly one-quarter of the large non-Iranian vessels stranded since the war began now having crossed the chokepoint, even as Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warned that ships continue to come under attack.

items.title: Ebola funding pledges nearly halved as outbreak spreads

featured_image.name: Ebola outbreak: What travel restrictions have countries ...

items.description:
International financial commitments to combat the Ebola outbreak in Central and East Africa have nearly halved in a matter of days, Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya revealed Thursday, as the deadly Bundibugyo strain continues to spread through the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda with no approved vaccine available.

Speaking from Kinshasa, Kaseya said pledges that stood at nearly $500 million on Monday, May 25, had dropped to approximately $290 million by Thursday after multiple donors withdrew their commitments. The collapse in funding represents a loss of roughly $210 million at a moment when the outbreak has grown to more than 1,000 suspected cases and 246 deaths in the DRC alone.[1][2][3]

items.title: Rubio thanks Pakistan for Iran mediation efforts
items.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the State Department on Friday, with discussions centering on Pakistan's role mediating the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and the broader bilateral relationship between Washington and Islamabad.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump's Situation Room meeting on Iran ends without deal

featured_image.name: Trump enters Situation Room to make 'final determination' on Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump convened a high-stakes meeting in the White House Situation Room on Friday to make what he called a "final determination" on a proposed memorandum of understanding with Iran, but the nearly two-hour session ended without a resolution, according to The New York Times.[1]

The meeting came after Trump announced his plans in a Truth Social post Friday morning, writing, "I will be meeting now, in the Situation Room, to make a final determination". He outlined preconditions for any agreement, insisting that Iran "must agree that they will never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb" and that the Strait of Hormuz must "immediately open" to unrestricted shipping with no tolls.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Chevron CEO says ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz this week

featured_image.name: Chevron CEO says Iran war impact isn't fully priced into oil ...

items.description: Chevron CEO Mike Wirth disclosed in an interview with Bloomberg TV that multiple vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz were attacked this week, including incidents not yet publicly reported, even as ceasefire optimism between the United States and Iran drove oil prices sharply lower.[1][2]

items.title: Trump announces lifting of naval blockade on Iran

featured_image.name: What we know about the US military's blockade of Iran

items.description: President Trump declared on Friday that the U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "will now be lifted," posting the announcement on Truth Social after convening in the White House Situation Room to make what officials described as a "final determination" on the deal with Iran. The announcement follows weeks of fraught negotiations and marks the most concrete step toward ending the nearly three-month conflict between the United States and Iran.[1][2]

items.title: China building 80-plus launch pads near nuclear silos

featured_image.name: China's Nuclear Acceleration Revealed in Satellite Images

items.description:
China is constructing a sprawling network of launch pads, bunkers, and communications nodes near its nuclear missile silos in the remote deserts of its northwest, according to a Reuters analysis of satellite imagery published on Friday.[1][2]

The images reveal more than 80 pads that could be used by China's expanding fleet of mobile missile launchers and air-defense batteries, along with facilities that may support electronic warfare, satellite communication, and command operations, according to three security experts who reviewed the imagery for Reuters.[2]
